representative_tasks.task: Orchestrate a daily feature-computation ETL with Airflow
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Airflow 3 DAG (schedule=, catchup=False) with retryable extract/transform/load tasks, a window anchored on data_interval_end with an exclusive end, bound SQL parameters, credentials from the environment, and intermediates on storage every worker can read

representative_tasks.task: Make the load step safe to retry
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Delete-then-insert of the as_of partition inside one transaction (or an upsert), so a retry leaves one copy and a failed insert rolls back the delete

representative_tasks.task: Add a data-quality gate before loading
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: A pandera schema validated with lazy=True plus an explicit empty-frame check, wired so load waits on validate

representative_tasks.task: Fix train/serve skew between a batch feature job and an online scoring path
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Diagnoses by comparing served vs offline feature values, then defines the features once in a feature store (Feast FeatureView over the published files, materialize-incremental, get_online_features at serving)

negative_cases: A window written as order_date BETWEEN ds-29 AND ds on Airflow 3, where ds is the fire date (planned misconception)
Turning on catchup=True for a DAG with a start_date a year in the past to fill history (planned edge_case)
rubric: Load tasks are idempotent (partition replace or upsert) and atomic; retries stay enabled
Train/serve skew is diagnosed with served-vs-offline feature comparisons before attributing degradation to drift
One feature definition backs both training and serving
Data-quality gate fails the run instead of loading bad data
Airflow-version-dependent semantics (ds vs data_interval_end, CLI names) are stated with the version they apply to
prerequisites: example-deps for executable tests: pandas, pyarrow, SQLAlchemy, pandera (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md); apache-airflow and feast are stubbed, not installed
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.

Executable tests need the example-test dependencies and run via run_evals.py --run-executable; they call the DAG's Python callables directly with hand-built Airflow 2/3-style contexts against a SQLite warehouse (the module ran in about 12 s as observed on 2026-10-27).
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: A customer_features table with exactly one row per (customer_id, as_of) after repeated loads
Per-partition feature parquet files published for the Feast FileSource
pandera SchemaErrors raised on negative spend or an empty feature file
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.

Hard-assertion robustness is spot-checked only: an independent reviewer's held-out probe found most realistic on-topic wrong answers passed the first-draft must_not_include patterns. The patterns were broadened and those answers committed verbatim as .fail.adversarial*/.pass.blind fixtures; later probes were written by the pattern author and are not blind.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
Airflow and Feast are stubbed in the executable tests, so scheduler behaviour (real retries, timetables, backfills) and online-store materialization are not exercised.
unsupported_use_cases: One-off cleaning/encoding of a single training dataset (data-preprocessing)
Monitoring a deployed model for drift (ml-monitoring)
